land.text: the ten southern states: 'South Sudan became an independent state on 9 July 2011' after the January 2011 referendum (98.83% for separation)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the split in 2014; the Sudan dossier moves it to July 2011 (republic-of-sudan_2011). Abyei, Heglig and Kafia Kingi are inside Cliopatria's Sudan shape, not this one.

capitals.name: Juba
capitals.note: 'It was planned that the capital city would be changed to the more centrally located Ramciel'; 'As of 2024, the relocation project is stalled.'

rulers.name: Salva Kiir Mayardit
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: First Vice-President and President of the Government of Southern Sudan from 11 August 2005; signed the constitution 'on Independence Day' (9 July 2011). Riek Machar was First Vice-President, sworn in again on 22 February 2020, and arrested on 26 March 2025.

correction.text: South Sudan from independence on 9 July 2011: Cliopatria's 2014 shape, unchanged, drawn three years earlier

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins South Sudan in 2014 although the infobox has 'Declared and recognised: 9 July 2011'. The Sudan dossier makes the matching correction (Sudan loses the south in July 2011, not 2014).

616,190 km2 against the infobox 644,329 km2 (ratio 0.96, fine). The gap is the disputed land: the gazetteer shows Cliopatria draws Abyei, the Heglig oilfield and Kafia Kingi inside its Sudan shape, not this one, so the ledger's contest events draw them as contested. The page says 'the Kafia Kingi area is disputed between South Sudan and Sudan' and 'the Ilemi Triangle is disputed between South Sudan and Kenya' but dates neither.
Identical to the 2014 shape; the page records no territorial change in 2024 (Abyei 'still remains disputed' as of March 2025).

region.text: Southern Sudan, the ten southern states

ledger.note: 2011: South Sudan becomes independent on 9 July. 'South Sudan became an independent state on 9 July 2011'; the referendum on 9-15 January 2011 gave 98.83% for separation. Infobox 'Declared and recognised: 9 July 2011'. The page gives no boundary; the land is Cliopatria's outline, without Abyei, Heglig and Kafia Kingi.

region.text: the Abyei Area, which Sudan 'seized control of' in May 2011 and which 'still remains disputed'

ledger.note: 2011: Abyei is claimed by both states from independence. Sudan had seized it in May 2011 ('with a force of approximately 5,000 soldiers', after 'an ambush by South Sudanese forces on May 19'); 'Following the advance South Sudan withdrew its forces from Abyei'; a militarisation deal on 20 June 2011 and UNISFA from 27 June 2011. The Sudan dossier opens the contest in May 2011, before South Sudan existed; this side opens it at independence. No end: the South Sudan page says 'an official referendum was never held' and 'As of March 2025, the region of Abyei still remains disputed'.

region.text: the Heglig oil fields, whose status 'remained linked to whether the area lay east or west of the 1931 administrative line'

ledger.note: 2012: South Sudanese forces hold Heglig. 'On 10 April Colonel Khalid Sawarmi, spokesman for the Sudanese army, claimed that South Sudanese forces had taken control of the Heglig oil fields' (the page also has Sudan's 26 March claim of an attack and South Sudan's withdrawal 'on 28 March'). The page presents the 10 April seizure as Sudan's claim; the South Sudan page has 'In March 2012, South Sudanese forces seized the Heglig oil fields'.

region.text: the Heglig oil fields, whose status 'remained linked to whether the area lay east or west of the 1931 administrative line'

ledger.note: 2012: South Sudan withdraws from Heglig. 'On April 20 Salva Kiir ordered his forces to withdraw from Heglig'; infobox territorial change 'South Sudanese withdrawal from Heglig', result 'Sudanese victory'. Agreements on borders and resources followed on 26-27 September 2012; Heglig stays in Sudan.

wars.name: Abyei crisis of May 2011

zones.text: the Abyei Area, which Sudan 'seized control of' in May 2011 and which 'still remains disputed'

wars.outcome: Sudan seized Abyei with about 5,000 soldiers; South Sudan withdrew its forces; a militarisation deal followed on 20 June 2011 and an Ethiopian UN force (UNISFA) deployed from 27 June 2011. The status stays disputed: no referendum was held.
wars.note: The event predates independence (the contestant was then the autonomous Southern Sudan); the page gives 'May 2011' and the 19 May ambush.

wars.name: Heglig Crisis

zones.text: the Heglig oil fields, whose status 'remained linked to whether the area lay east or west of the 1931 administrative line'

wars.outcome: Sudanese victory: South Sudanese forces withdrew from Heglig after the 20 April order; eight agreements were signed at Addis Ababa on 27 September 2012 (the infobox says 26 September).
wars.note: Infobox dates 26 March - 26 September 2012 along the whole border; Teshwin was attacked by Sudanese forces on 9 April, and Jau in Unity state 'was occupied by Sudanese forces' in early December 2011 (no end date on the page, so no occupation event is recorded).

wars.name: South Sudanese Civil War
wars.outcome: 'South Sudan descended into the South Sudanese Civil War from 2013 to 2018'; a peace agreement was signed in August 2015, a power-sharing agreement came into effect in August 2018 and Kiir and Machar agreed another deal on 20 February 2020.
wars.note: The page names no rebel-held town or date: only a map caption 'Under control of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-in-Opposition'. No zone is drawn; the rebels need a dossier from another agent.

certainty.note: The frontier with Sudan follows an administrative line ('the 1931 administrative line' is the test for Heglig) and the 2012 agreements 'on borders and natural resources'; the disputed exceptions, drawn soft, are the Abyei Area, Heglig, Kafia Kingi (disputed with Sudan) and the Ilemi Triangle (disputed with Kenya).

notes: Page budget 1-2: both opened; the title 'Sudan-South Sudan border conflict' returned url_not_found and Heglig Crisis was read instead. (1) Cliopatria's South Sudan starts in 2014, the Sudan row shrinks in 2014; independence was 9 July 2011, so the dossier starts in July 2011 with a new keyframe south-sudan_2011 (2011-2013). (2) Abyei: the contest_start has no contest_end by design (the page says the dispute persists to 2025); the validator warns about the unpaired start. The Sudan dossier opens the same zone in May 2011. (3) Heglig: the South Sudan page says March 2012, the Heglig Crisis page 10 April (Sudan's claim) and withdrawal 20 April; the ledger follows the Heglig Crisis page, matching the Sudan dossier. (4) Kafia Kingi and the Ilemi Triangle are 'disputed' on the South Sudan page without dates, so no event is recorded. (5) The Civil War (2013-2018, SPLM-IO under Riek Machar) held land but the page names none: a rebel dossier for the SPLM-IO is needed from another agent. (6) The 14-Mile area, Kiir Adem and Kaka/Jodha are not on any page opened. (7) Abyei and Heglig have no place names in the gazetteer, so coordinates are used (the same as the Sudan dossier).
